decisions.reason: The rye country bread remains very close to the bakery’s core bread-making knowledge and, with no clear adverse signal after another year, management would continue it and rely on incremental refinement rather than withdrawal.
As a flagship premium raisin stollen with a gold-medal quality signal and a strong fit with established seasonal confectionery capabilities, it is highly unlikely to be removed.
The rye mixed bread with seeds builds directly on existing recipes, processes, and customer demand patterns, so the firm can absorb feedback easily and has little reason to discontinue it.

Although the dark barley malt rye bread is somewhat more niche than standard loaves, it still rests on familiar baking competences and is more likely to be adjusted within the range than dropped outright.
The marzipan Christmas stollen is closely related to the firm’s proven stollen know-how and complements the successful seasonal line, leaving only a moderate range-rationalisation risk.
